title: Airport construction bids with posted results (2026)
question: For the Airport construction jobs whose bids are posted, how many firms bid, how did the lowest bid compare with the estimate, and are the bidders the usual Airport firms?
finding: The Airport's procurement portal lists 10 closed construction solicitations; bid results are posted for 3. 12184.51 (As-Needed Agreement: Airfield Electrical Testing, Repairs an): 1 bid, lowest BASS Electric at $5.7 million against an engineer's estimate of $5.0 million (113%); 10672.61 (5kV Cable Replacement in Field Lighting Building (FLB) No. 2): 4 bids, lowest TJ Gardner Company at $2.5 million against an engineer's estimate of $5.1 million (49%); 11939.61 (NIP, EEI 2024 Phase, Group 1): 4 bids, lowest Pro-Ex Contstruction, Inc. at $644,000 against an engineer's estimate of $748,736 (86%). The only bidder on 12184.51, BASS Electric, was prime on 6 Airport contracts in the Controller's file, the latest with a like title being AIR11643.50;ASNAirfield Elec. (2021). 2 bidders on the same job also appear as prime and subcontractor to one another on other Airport contracts. Each portal entry says "Awarded" but the files do not say to whom.
how: Bidder names, total bid prices, the engineer's estimate and the local-business discounts are read from each abstract of bids (pdftotext). The engineer's estimate in the abstract includes allowances; the bid-opening slides give the same figure, or for 11939.61 the figure without its $23,000 of allowances. Bidders are matched by name to the Controller's payment and contract files, the City's certified local-business directory and the State disadvantaged-business directory.
limits: Three jobs are a small sample, and the portal holds only 2026 solicitations. A single bid on an as-needed contract, or a low bid far under the estimate, has ordinary causes: specialised airfield work that few firms do, a soft estimate, or a bidder who misread the work (the City can reject a bid that is too low to be responsible). Abstracts list bids as read; they do not show responsiveness reviews or who was awarded. Home addresses in the noise-insulation abstract are not shown.
